overview.title: Banking In India Scheduled Commercial Banks
overview.definition: Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs) in India comprise all banks included in the Second Schedule of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Act, 1934, satisfying criteria of minimum paid-up capital and reserves, and ensuring operations do not adversely affect depositors' interests.
overview.importanceInUpsc: Crucial for UPSC Prelims (RBI Act provisions, bank categorization, priority sector lending, capital adequacy norms) and GS Paper III Mains (financial inclusion, banking sector reforms, NPAs, bad bank, digital banking).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Banking In India Scheduled Commercial Banks.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of monetary policy, financial intermediaries, and the central bank.

sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Second Schedule Status**: Banks must be included in the **Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934**, fulfilling mandatory statutory requirements.
• **Minimum Capital Requirement**: An aggregate paid-up capital and collected reserves of not less than **Rs. 5 crore** is mandatory.
• **Regulatory Oversight**: Directly regulated by the **RBI** under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
• **Key Function**: Mobilizing public deposits and providing credit to various sectors including agriculture, industry, and services, alongside statutory obligations like **CRR** and **SLR**.

items.definition: Scheduled banks enjoy the right to borrow from the RBI for emergency/liquidity purposes (Repo/Bank Rate) and are bound by statutory reserve ratios. Non-scheduled banks do not qualify for these privileges.

Mandatory lending targets imposed by RBI on SCBs to ensure adequate credit flow to vulnerable sectors like Agriculture, MSMEs, Export Credit, Education, Housing, Social Infrastructure, and Renewable Energy.
Also known as Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR), it measures a bank's capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets, adhering strictly to Basel III norms to absorb losses.
RBI framework that allows supervisory intervention for SCBs that breach critical thresholds of capital, asset quality (NPAs), and profitability.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Financial Capitals & Metros**: Mumbai, NCR (Delhi), Bengaluru, and Chennai host major corporate headquarters and treasury operations of SCBs.
• **Credit-Deposit (CD) Ratio Disparities**: Southern and Western states typically show higher CD ratios, whereas Eastern and North-Eastern states experience lower credit uptake relative to deposits mobilized, indicating regional financial exclusion.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Stressed assets (NPAs), twin balance sheet problem, cyber security risks, and governance lapses in both public and private sectors.
• **Policy Interventions**: Establishment of National Asset Reconstruction Company Limited (NARCL) / Bad Bank, PSB consolidation (mergers), IBC (Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code), and Digital Banking Units (DBUs).

items.title: Mnemonic for RRB Shareholding Pattern
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: "Centi-State-Sponsor" -> 50:15:35
• **Decoded Meaning**: **Cen**tral Government = 50%, **State** Government = 15%, **Sponsor** Bank = 35%.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly eliminates incorrect numerical options in matching questions.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: SCBs = PSBs + Private Banks + Foreign Banks + RRBs. All must be listed in the 2nd Schedule of RBI Act 1934.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often states that 'Cooperative banks are Scheduled Commercial Banks.' This is false. While some cooperative banks are scheduled (Scheduled State/Urban Cooperative Banks), they are NOT commercial banks. Commercial banks focus on profit-making and cater to general commercial needs, distinct from cooperative principles.

Mains Value Addition: Quote the Indradhanush Roadmap for PSBs, EASE reforms index (Enhanced Access and Service Excellence), and Basel III capital implementation timelines to fetch extra marks in GS Paper III banking questions.

keyTakeaways: Scheduled Commercial Banks must feature in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934, possessing a minimum paid-up capital of Rs. 5 crore.
SCBs comprise four distinct pillars: Public Sector Banks, Private Sector Banks, Foreign Banks, and Regional Rural Banks.
Rigorous statutory compliance (CRR, SLR, PSL, Basel III CRAR) differentiates SCBs from non-scheduled entities and ensures macroeconomic stability.
